## Purpose and product boundary
This monorepo contains the AutoGPT Platform: a managed or self-hosted system for building, deploying, triggering, and observing AI-agent workflows. Its primary product combines a visual workflow builder, agent library/marketplace, conversational Copilot/AutoPilot, scheduled or webhook-driven execution, and integrations. The separate `classic/` tree preserves the older standalone agent, Forge framework, and benchmark tooling.

## Primary entry points
- Platform frontend: Next.js application rooted at `autogpt_platform/frontend/src/app/layout.tsx`, with principal routes for builder, Copilot, library, marketplace, and team surfaces.
- Platform backend: Python application at `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/app.py`; REST and WebSocket API composition are at `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/api/rest_api.py` and `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/api/ws_api.py`.
- Self-hosted deployment: Docker-based single-container launcher at `autogpt_platform/single-container/entrypoint.sh`.
- Legacy applications have independent Python module entry points: `classic/original_autogpt/autogpt/__main__.py`, `classic/forge/forge/__main__.py`, and `classic/direct_benchmark/direct_benchmark/__main__.py`.

## Workflow authoring and reusable agents
The builder represents an agent as a persisted graph of typed blocks, nodes, connections, inputs, and versions. The frontend flow editor maintains client graph/node/edge state and saves or executes graphs; the backend graph data model and builder routes enforce the server boundary.
- `autogpt_platform/frontend/src/app/(platform)/build/page.tsx`
- `autogpt_platform/frontend/src/app/(platform)/build/components/FlowEditor/Flow/Flow.tsx`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/data/graph.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/api/features/builder/routes.py`

The library and marketplace turn graphs into reusable, installable agents, with versions, presets, folders, searches, and publishing/review workflows.
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/api/features/library/db.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/api/features/store/routes.py`
- `autogpt_platform/frontend/src/app/(platform)/library/page.tsx`

## Execution runtime and eventing
A run is queued/scheduled, executes a graph’s blocks, records execution and cost state, and exposes progress/results back to clients. The executor is a distinct asynchronous runtime from HTTP API handling; Redis and RabbitMQ modules indicate queue/event-bus boundaries. Human review, billing limits, credentials, and activity events are part of run control.
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/executor/manager.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/executor/scheduler.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/data/execution.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/data/event_bus.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/data/rabbitmq.py`

## Block and integration boundary
Blocks are the extensibility unit: they encapsulate LLM calls, control flow, data transforms, external APIs, webhooks, media/code execution, and nested-agent orchestration. Base block abstractions and registry behavior separate graph execution from provider-specific implementations. OAuth, scoped/managed credentials, credential leasing, and webhook managers isolate secrets and inbound third-party events.
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/blocks/_base.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/blocks/llm.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/blocks/orchestrator.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/integrations/creds_manager.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/integrations/webhooks/_base.py`

## Copilot, experts, and memory
Copilot is a conversational orchestration layer that streams model responses and tool activity, can create/edit/run agents and blocks, delegate to experts, and retain context. Its queued turn processor is separate from web chat delivery. Graphiti supplies graph-oriented memory ingestion, search, reranking, and persistence through a FalkorDB driver.
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/copilot/service.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/copilot/turn_queue.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/copilot/tools/agent_generator/pipeline.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/copilot/graphiti/ingest.py`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/backend/copilot/graphiti/falkordb_driver.py`

## Client/API/auth boundary
The TypeScript frontend uses Next.js route handlers as an authentication/proxy/streaming edge in front of the Python backend. Copilot streaming has a dedicated server route and client transport/store. Auth supports application sessions and a Supabase bridge; backend shared auth utilities authorize API access and permissions.
- `autogpt_platform/frontend/src/app/api/proxy/[...path]/route.ts`
- `autogpt_platform/frontend/src/app/api/chat/sessions/[sessionId]/stream/route.ts`
- `autogpt_platform/frontend/src/app/(platform)/copilot/copilotStreamTransport.ts`
- `autogpt_platform/frontend/src/lib/auth/auth.ts`
- `autogpt_platform/autogpt_libs/autogpt_libs/auth/service.py`

## Persistence, infrastructure, and operations
The platform schema and migrations target a relational database with vector-search-related migrations; local DB Docker assets are Supabase-oriented. Runtime infrastructure includes PostgreSQL/Supabase, Redis, RabbitMQ, FalkorDB, object/cloud storage, Docker, Nginx, and optional single-container supervision. External services include LLM providers, OAuth-connected applications, Stripe billing/webhooks, email/push delivery, and observability/analytics integrations.
- `autogpt_platform/backend/schema.prisma`
- `autogpt_platform/backend/migrations/`
- `autogpt_platform/db/docker/docker-compose.yml`
- `autogpt_platform/docker-compose.platform.yml`
- `autogpt_platform/single-container/supervisor/supervisord.conf`
